text: What do MAC flooding, ARP spoofing, VLAN hopping, rogue DHCP and STP attacks have in common?
choices: They all require physical access to a switch
Each exploits a protocol designed to be helpful and trusting on a local segment, and each mitigation is a free switch feature that is off by default
They are all defeated by encryption
explanation: Port security, DAI, native VLAN hygiene, DHCP snooping and BPDU Guard would eliminate all five, cost nothing but configuration time, and are absent from a large proportion of production networks.
